subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should skill lifecycle management be a core Skill Workshop feature, a plugin/ClawHub extension enabled by new core hooks, or split so only missing hooks land in core?
rationale: The request would add automatic learning behavior, skill visibility changes, persistent metrics, and new config, so automation cannot choose the ownership and consent boundary safely.

options.title: Design hooks and split lifecycle policy
options.body: Define the minimal core events/state needed for plugins or a future sponsored core workflow, then separately decide archive/delete UX and storage semantics before implementation.

options.title: Build directly into core Skill Workshop
options.body: Accept Skill Workshop as the owner of failure repair and retirement, with explicit config, migration/doctor coverage, and conservative default-off behavior.

options.title: Route to ClawHub/plugin only
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core unchanged unless a plugin implementation proves a missing extension API that maintainers want to support.

recommendation.title: Design hooks and split lifecycle policy
recommendation.body: Define the minimal core events/state needed for plugins or a future sponsored core workflow, then separately decide archive/delete UX and storage semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the most recent current-main Skill Workshop/Skill Research lines and is the best routing candidate for product-boundary decisions around this subsystem.
